correctness.rationale: The proof is exact for independent equal-variance Gaussian row readings and an unrelaxed one-step identity-system update. Rotate the two residuals to independent Gaussian sums and differences; the greedy selection event is their sign product. Its probability yields the split risk. The squared-noise difference factors into independent Gaussian truncated moments, giving the exact isotropic reuse penalty. Strict logarithmic concavity of a positive erf-weight factor proves the unique sharp angular maximizer; the scalar crossover is unique by monotonicity. The extracted independent conditional quadrature and deterministic checks corroborate every boundary and equality case, without being treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Residual ranking and projection often reuse the same noisy observation; the theorem isolates its exact nonzero error tax from the benefit of selecting a more informative row. The sharp 1.240125... noise-normalized boundary classifies when maximal-residual greed loses to uniform sampling for every start, while the split implementation removes that reversal. The complete fixed-radius orientation envelope identifies exactly the worst and best starting directions, providing a natural robustness benchmark for noisy row-action methods. The scope is intentionally one-step and two-row, not advertised as general algorithm complexity.
